subject: MADT
descr: The Art of Cinema and Television
notes:
The Art of Cinema and Television: Cowboys and Gangsters

The Western and the Gangster film genres are two of the most popular and influential genres in film and television history. The Western's mythic morality tales often explore the frontier of an imagined, idealized American past where good and lawfulness faces off against evil and chaos. Gangster films, by contrast, offer amoral fantasies where violent antiheroes celebrate the chaos, corruption, and injustices of urban city life. Yet, despite these apparent differences in ideology, form, and narrative structure, both genres offer similar mythic explorations of the violent, chaotic, racist, and often existential undercurrents at work in American culture. This class will explore this linkage. Lectures examine how each genre uses characters, plots, themes, and iconography to comment on the formation and ideological legacy of American society. Each class will screen one film (alternating Westerns and Gangster) from the classical, postclassical, revisionist, postmodern, and/or neoclassical eras of the Hollywood studio system. Students will be asked to produce original insights into how both westerns and gangster films function and how the genres have reframed themselves in countries such as Italy, Hong Kong, and Australia.

notes: This course explores the theory and practice of first-year learning with peer-to-peer mentorship as the focus. Participants explore current research on learning theory, emerging adulthood, communities of practice, and strategies for guiding students in the transition to college. The course is collaborative and interactive. Peer mentors will examine their own self-awareness, develop learning skills and strategies, and explore methods for facilitating such skills in their future mentees. Participants will review empirical research on the first-year experience and the complex transition from high-school to college, as well as reflect on their own experiences in order to develop the most supportive mentor-mentee relationship.
